term: Illustrative Work Transformation / Weighted Propagation Matrix
statement: The WTM/propagation model is an illustrative test harness for evaluating the Predictive Program Management 2.0 architecture. Its weights are evidence-calibrated ordinal values and synthetic assumptions, not historically calibrated probabilities.
orientation: W[i, j]: row i = source / upstream node, column j = target / downstream node (DSM convention, unchanged)
equation: x(t+1) = W^T x(t), i.e. x_j(t+1) = sum_i W[i, j] * x_i(t)
raw_behaviour_explanation: Spectral radius < 1: under repeated application of W^T, any initial disturbance eventually decays geometrically, at a long-run rate of about the spectral radius per step. Short-run growth is still possible, because the largest out-strength (row sum of W) exceeds 1.
max_out_strength_note: = ||W^T||_1, the largest possible one-step growth of the total (L1) disturbance.
dominant_mode_note: Eigenvector of W^T for the dominant eigenvalue, scaled to sum to 1: the long-run shape of a decaying disturbance that reaches the D4/D6 loop.
